recognize_zh: 背景中散佈大量短胖的藍色桿菌，並可見被嗜中性球與單核細胞吞噬的細胞內桿菌；紅血球內有 Howell-Jolly 小體（箭頭）及刺狀紅血球，提示無脾狀態下的革蘭氏陰性桿菌敗血症。
features: Numerous extracellular short, plump, blue-staining bacilli scattered throughout the smear background
Intracellular bacilli within a neutrophil (lower left) and within a vacuole of a mononuclear cell (top)
Howell-Jolly bodies in red cells (arrows), consistent with asplenia
Marked poikilocytosis with echinocytic/spiculated cells, teardrop forms and polychromatic red cells
A small dense nucleated cell with adherent bacilli (right), likely a nucleated red cell
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows abundant extracellular short bacilli throughout the film, with phagocytosed bacilli in a neutrophil and in a vacuole of a mononuclear cell. Red cells show poikilocytosis with spiculated cells, teardrop forms and polychromasia, and Howell-Jolly bodies are present (arrows), indicating hyposplenism or asplenia. Bacteremia of this magnitude visible on a routine smear indicates overwhelming sepsis; in a patient with pyruvate kinase deficiency and asplenia, the findings are consistent with fulminant gram-negative bacillary sepsis (Klebsiella pneumoniae on culture). Gram stain and blood culture are needed for organism identification.

ddx.dx: Stain precipitate or contaminating bacteria in stain/water
ddx.vs: Contaminants lie on top of cells in varying focal planes and are never phagocytosed, whereas here bacilli are clearly within neutrophil vacuoles.
Capnocytophaga appears as thin fusiform elongated rods, whereas these are short plump bacilli; culture identifies the organism.
Pappenheimer bodies are clustered small granules within red cells that are Prussian blue positive, unlike the single round Howell-Jolly bodies and extracellular rods.
Debris is irregular and variably sized, lacking the uniform rod morphology and intracellular phagocytosis of bacteria.
